source.title: RUB: Evaluating Residual Knowledge in Unlearned Models

record.file_problem: Whole paper and supplementary material are present; the text is not visibly garbled or cut off.
record.tranche_reason: Tests recovery of unlearned information after attacks, using computer-vision tasks and input-mapping attacks rather than the LLM unlearning and attacks in the claim's original sources.
record.gate_note: The study tests image-classification, image-reconstruction, and text-to-image unlearning under its Unlearning Mapping Attack (UMA). The text-to-image attack optimizes adversarial textual prompts; the other attacks modify image inputs. It does not test LLM unlearning, fine-tuning recovery, internal activation edits, or quantization. T2I table entries also report average/median attack steps; those are omitted under the 60-row limit. Other omitted measures include MIA and image-generation IS/FID, which do not directly report the recovery accuracy/attack success rate catalogued here.
record.test_reason: The study gives pre- and post-attack recovery rates for unlearned models, but in computer vision rather than LLMs: ResNet50 class unlearning, MAE inpainting and diffusion-model concept erasure. Its attack, UMA, is a white-box, worst-case input attack that uses the original model and the forget samples. It is not a simple attack. That makes this a new setting (T3), not the same question by a different method (T2).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that current unlearning methods often fail to fully erase information and are vulnerable to adversarial recovery, even when they pass standard metrics. They add that retraining stays robust in class unlearning, and they call for robustness as a core requirement.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates diverse computer-vision unlearning methods using UMA, a white-box optimized input attack; it does not reproduce the cited LLM unlearning recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Attack strength and dataset complexity affect classification results; UMA step count and step size affect attack efficacy; T2I results vary by unlearning method and target concept.
record.code_released: not stated; the paper says the codebase and checkpoints will be published.
record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR) Workshops, June 2026, pages 8550-8559
record.problems: The evaluation uses a white-box, worst-case attacker with access to original and unlearned models and forget samples. Generative-task retraining baselines are absent. UMA optimization is non-convex and the authors state it does not guarantee exploration of all perturbations. Table 3 reports ASR and attack-step summaries but not uncertainty estimates. Classifier-based ASR is used for T2I attack success.
record.rows_left_out: Within the 60-row cap, omitted the T2I average/median attack-step result for each of the 35 method/concept cells in Table 3; retained the ASR result for each. Also omitted MIA rows and IS/FID rows, which are additional measures not needed to record the direct recovery-rate outcomes prioritized here.

untested.parts: LLM unlearning such as WMDP/RMU or Harry Potter, and 'simple' attacks. Only white-box, optimised UMA/UnlearnDiffAtk attacks with access to the original model are used.
All of B: no relearning by fine-tuning.
All of C: no activation-direction ablation or analysis of blocking versus deletion.
LLM rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages and in-context information. Only gradient-optimised text prompts on diffusion models are tested.
Only AdvUnlearn (diffusion, adversarial training) against one optimised-prompt attack. No LLM counter-method, and no fine-tuning or other attacks.

missing.what: Class-unlearning UA/MIA at 16/255. RL and SalUn on CIFAR10 rise to about 27% UA, CIFAR100 RL/SalUn to 80–85%, and retrain stays at 0.

Instance-level unlearning. Even the retrained model reaches about 99.98% UA under the 8/255 attack, so UMA cannot separate true forgetting from adversarial misclassification in this setting. This is a validity caveat for the classifier rows.
Average/median attack steps per T2I cell. AdvUnlearn and Scissorhands mostly reach the 100-step cap. This was declared omitted but is decisive for F.
missing.locator: Table 3, second line of each cell

record.verdict_notes: The reader labelled F 'challenges' and I2I 'supports' A; both are reversed here. AdvUnlearn largely resists the attack, and the I2I rows show recovery, which challenges A. Retrain rows are valid controls. Because the setting is vision rather than LLM, these verdicts transfer to the LLM claim only by analogy. The attacks are strong white-box attacks, not the simple attacks that A names. The record's peer_reviewed field (CVPR Workshops 2026) is not supported by the text, which shows only arXiv v2.

versions.untested_parts: The paper tests computer-vision unlearning and recovery under UMA, not LLM methods or the full set of methods named in the claim. Its attacks are optimized input attacks, not necessarily simple attacks. It does not establish that targeted accuracy was near chance for every tested method.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning on unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten examples.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis of access-blocking versus deletion.
Tests optimized adversarial prompts for text-to-image models, not LLM prompt rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information.
Tests AdvUnlearn among its text-to-image methods, but does not test a counter-method against every attack type in the claim.

statements.correction: RUB: ResNet50 class unlearning, not an LLM. White-box UMA image attack, CIFAR10. RL forget-set UA 0±0 -> 5.82±5.23 at 8/255 and 26.64±18.28 at 16/255. SalUn 0±0 -> 7.13±9.59 and 26.87±16.39. One attack type, white-box access only.
statements.problem: All its findings are LLM results from other papers; it says nothing about RUB. The cited row C10-RL (8/255 only) can't show the attack-type, access or strength factor by itself. RUB uses one white-box attack and shows only a strength effect, at 16/255.

statements.correction: UMA post-attack ASR: ESD 0.44-0.907, SPM 0.82-1, FMN 0.96-1. EraseDiff and SalUn reach 0.5-0.88 on Church, Garbage Truck and Parachute, but 0.059-0.246 on Nudity and Tench. ASR is classifier-based.
statements.problem: Correct. Caveats: RUB doesn't name SD v1.4 (it uses UnlearnDiffAtk's checkpoints). Its T2I results have no retrain control and no uncertainty; controls and uncertainty apply only to its classification results.
